subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH Item-3 -- THE canonical projection loader. Reads the Iceberg graph_nodes + graph_edges tables at the Nessie branch head and projects them into a local Kuzu DB (CloudNode / CloudEdge) for cross-layer Cypher traversal. Unlike kuzu_load.py (snapshot-tarball, nodes only) it reads the tables themselves, so it includes incremental commits made since the last nightly snapshot, and it loads the EDGE set.

as_of.graph_vintage: Pins at RUN time to the branch-head marker s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph/warehouse/_branch_head.main.json, measured live this session at LastModified 2026-08-30T02:11:47Z -- 2 s before the AWS snapshot tarball (02:11:49Z) that its sibling producer reads. The marker names the graph_nodes / graph_edges metadata_location the run actually loads.

methodology.how: main() reads the writer-stamped branch-head marker via _provenance.read_branch_head_marker() and takes the graph_nodes / graph_edges metadata_location from it (the HEAD oracle). If the marker is absent it prints WARN: HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN and falls back to latest_table_metadata(), a paginated newest-*.metadata.json-by-mtime scan. Each table is read whole through pyiceberg StaticTable.from_metadata(...).scan().to_arrow(). Nodes dedup into `best` on (arn if non-empty else node_id), keeping the highest snapshot_ts and COUNTING key collisions. With --force (the DEFAULT) the existing Kuzu DB is dropped -- file or directory, plus its .wal -- and a surviving path raises SystemExit rather than proceeding. Nodes are MERGEd, then edges, with endpoints required to exist in `best`; missing-endpoint edges are COUNTED AND SKIPPED, never stubbed. Edge MERGE keys on {edge_type, props} because props is part of edge identity (CTO 225614Z). An untyped-node check, a per-layer summary, a provenance manifest write, and the comp_detect TSGRAPH fold gate follow; rc is 0 only when untyped == 0 and the gate did not block.

stages_inferential: the FALLBACK pin only: latest_table_metadata() treats newest-*.metadata.json-by-mtime as HEAD, which the code's own comment marks RETIRED because mtime-newest can be an orphaned-commit artifact (CVO dc06744c6). It is inferential, it is NOT the active path (the marker resolved live this session), and when taken the run announces it.

persistence.form: A Kuzu database at --db (default infra/aws/globgrph/kuzu_nessie_db), materialized by Kuzu as either a directory or a single file depending on version -- the wipe path handles both. Two tables: CloudNode(node_id PK, arn, node_type, name, layer, drift_class, source, snapshot_ts, props) and CloudEdge(FROM CloudNode TO CloudNode, edge_type, layer, snapshot_ts, props). A provenance manifest is written BESIDE the DB carrying source_kind=nessie, both snapshot ids, both metadata keys and their LastModified, the warehouse bucket/prefix, and node/edge counts.
persistence.evidence: DEFAULT_DB_PATH at kuzu_nessie_load.py:42; table DDL :134-141; both-shapes wipe :125-129; manifest fields :213-229. Classified 'projection' not 'source' deliberately: every value it holds is read from the Iceberg tables, which remain the authority -- the DB is rebuilt from them and holds nothing not recoverable from the marker plus the warehouse. That is the exact opposite of its sibling derive_stitch.py, which DERIVES edges existing nowhere else and is therefore a source.

key.identity_space: MIXED WITHIN ONE COLUMN BY DESIGN. The Kuzu primary key node_id is set to `arn if non-empty else node_id`, because comp_aws_cli keys EDGES by ARN while a node's own `id` is the short name with the ARN in a separate column. The PK column therefore holds ARNs for AWS-plane nodes and short names for everything else, and edge endpoints must be expressed in the same mixed space to match.
key.key_expression: TWO DIFFERENT EXPRESSIONS, and they are NOT symmetric -- stating them separately because asserting one rule for both is false against the pinned writer. (1) NODE MEMBER KEY, kuzu_nessie_load.py:150 verbatim: `key = (row.get('arn') or '').strip() or (row.get('node_id') or '').strip()` -- i.e. STRIPPED arn if non-empty after stripping, else STRIPPED node_id. Rows yielding an empty key are dropped (:151-152). On collision the higher snapshot_ts wins. (2) EDGE ENDPOINT KEYS, :184 verbatim: `src, dst = row.get('src_id') or '', row.get('dst_id') or ''` -- RAW src_id / dst_id or empty string, with NO .strip() and NO arn-or-id fallback. Those raw strings are then membership-tested VERBATIM against the computed node-key set `best` (:185), and an endpoint absent from it increments `skipped` and drops the edge (:186-187). ⛔ THE ARMS ARE DISTINGUISHABLE BY A WHITESPACE-BEARING ENDPOINT: the node expression would strip it into the key set, the edge path compares the unstripped string, misses, and silently counts a skip. A consumer computing edge endpoint keys with the node rule would predict a match the writer does not make.
key.declared_mapping: Declared and justified in an inline comment at :145-149 ('the Kuzu PK is arn-if-present else node_id'), with the dedup rule (newest snapshot_ts wins per key) in the same block. The docstring's Schema section (:19-24) declares the column list but NOT this key rule -- the rule lives only in the implementation comment.

The instrument that would answer it already exists and prints on every run (key_collisions=), so this is MEASURABLE HERE AND UNMEASURED BY ME, not fine-by-default.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: LOUD ALMOST EVERYWHERE, which makes this substrate materially safer than its sibling. Missing branch-head marker -> printed WARN: HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN plus an explicit fallback (the degrade ANNOUNCES itself). No metadata.json for a table prefix -> SystemExit naming the prefix. --force unable to remove the DB -> SystemExit rather than a MERGE into a half-wiped DB (this exact hazard was once observed: 1967 nodes from a 1180-row table after a Windows file-lock rmtree failure). Edge endpoints missing -> counted and skipped, never stubbed. Untyped nodes -> OK/ERROR line and rc=1. A NEW un-baselined fold-gate finding -> BLOCKED, promotion halted, rc=1, with an audited COMP_DETECT_GATE_OVERRIDE escape. THE ONE FAIL-OPEN: comp_detect raising internally is caught by a bare `except Exception` at :253 which prints WARN: TSGRAPH fold gate could not run (<err>) and does NOT block -- deliberate and documented ('a gate crash must not block a valid graph'), and it PRINTS, so it is visible in a log. A SECOND, quieter one: _provenance.read_branch_head_marker swallows every failure into None, so 'marker absent', 'S3 unreachable' and 'unparseable JSON' become one value -- the caller still announces UNKNOWN, so the DEGRADE is distinguishable while its CAUSE is not.
silent_degrade_paths: an all-empty-key node batch would be skipped by the `if not key: continue` guard at :150-151 with no counter incremented -- the only uncounted drop in the file
comp_detect gate raising internally -> gate does not run, rc stays 0; visible only as a WARN line, so a caller reading rc alone sees a clean load with no gate
read_branch_head_marker's bare except (_provenance.py:133-142) collapses absent / unreachable / malformed into None -- the fallback is announced but the reason is lost

verdict.why: This is the better-built of the two load-bearing writers and the card should say so plainly: it announces its own degrade instead of hiding it (HEAD-ORACLE UNKNOWN), hard-fails rather than proceeding on a partial wipe after that exact corruption was once observed, counts and reports every drop it makes instead of reconciling it away, keeps props in edge identity so distinct edges cannot collapse last-wins, and ends on a fold gate that actually HALTS promotion rather than warning. Its primary pin resolved live at carding. QUALIFIED, not SOUND, on three points, and the first will bite a reader: (1) DECLARATIVE DRIFT -- the module docstring at :10-18 still presents newest-metadata-by-mtime as THE pinning mechanism, while the code retired it to a fallback and its own inline comment cites the CVO finding that mtime-newest can be an orphaned-commit artifact; the docstring is what a reader meets first and it describes a mechanism that is no longer primary. (2) One uncounted drop: the empty-key guard at :150-151 is the single skip in the file with no counter beside it, in a file whose whole discipline is counting its skips. (3) The key space is mixed within one PK column by design and its stability is MEASURABLE by the collision counter the code already prints, but UNMEASURED here because this lane did not execute the loader -- recorded as key_is_stable 'unknown' with the row basis dropped to 'absent' rather than guessed. None of the three requires redesign; (1) is a documentation edit.
blocking_defects: NODE and EDGE key rules are ASYMMETRIC: node keys are stripped ARN-or-node_id (:150), edge endpoints are raw src_id/dst_id with no strip and no fallback (:184) compared verbatim to the node-key set (:185). A whitespace-bearing endpoint is stripped into the key set by the node rule and MISSED by the edge rule, silently incrementing skipped_missing_endpoint.
